column1: # SQL columns of each table, as agreed with the maintainer (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-19).
# One line per column, in printed order. A header the extractor reads must match these
# labels, or the table is refused: a renamed or added column is a decision, not a guess.
# table: the table key. col: the SQL column. type:
#   text    printed text, kept as printed
#   amount  a printed amount, parsed exactly (Decimal); a dash is NULL
#   number  a printed count or quantity, parsed exactly
#   code    an identity (`016`, `92956`): kept as printed, leading zeros matter
#   group   the heading printed once above a group of rows (MAE operator); carried onto them
#   carry   text printed in its column on a group's first row only (MEF II `Ditta`); carried
#           down to the rows under it, up to the group's `<name> Totale` subtotal, which must
#           name the same (maintainer, 2026-10-20: the table is a visualisation, not raw data)
#   link    not printed: on each item, the `row_ord` of the row whose amount covers it.
#           sum field `<amount col> <item col> <opener col>`: a row printing <opener>
#           opens a unit (MAE A1: an authorisation, its date); in a unit with as many
#           amounts as items the k-th amount goes with the k-th item, else an amount
#           covers the item on its line and those under it, up to the next amount. A row
#           with an amount and no item continues the item above: its text from <item col>
#           rightwards moves there, the amount's side stays. More amounts than items: an
#           amount line with no item gets the item above's text and codes (not its
#           quantity), flagged `copied from row N`, and is a row of its own. No amount: each
#           item gets an amount of 0, nothing printed (`_raw` NULL), flagged. Anything else
#           links nothing and is an issue (maintainer, 2026-10-21, A1 matching page).
#   unit    not printed: on each row, the `row_ord` of the row that opens
#           its unit (MAE A1: the dated line of its authorisation). Derived, not an
#           official number: A1 prints none (maintainer, 2026-10-21). In a table with no
#           `link`, the sum field names the column whose printed value opens the unit
#           (MEF: `numero_autorizzazione`); a unit listed first opens the ones after it
#           (N1: a new operator opens a new licence)
#   Rule (maintainer, 2026-10-21): a table whose rows nest (lines under one printed unit)
#   gets a `riga_*` column naming each row's unit, so the nesting is never lost; `riga_`
#   marks a row of the same table, never a value or code the report prints.
#   Nested = the layout shows the grouping. A table printing every line complete is flat,
#   even if lines share a key the print does not show (Dogane M): no id (DECISIONS.md).
#   A `riga_*` value is a `row_ord`: unique only with `year` (the edition, on every row of
#   every table), as the rows of one year's table. Across years the key is (year, riga_*):
#   `WHERE year = 2025 AND riga_autorizzazione = 2`, joins `ON ... AND a.year = i.year`. It
#   never follows an authorisation from one edition to the next: A1 and F1 print no number
#   company not printed: ArmTrace's id of the company named in the column the sum field
#           gives (`lib/companies.py`; names: lib/data/company-names.tsv), NULL with an
#           issue when the name has none yet (maintainer, 2026-10-21, plan.md Phase 3)
#   block   a label printed once in a cell spanning a block of rows (T13's rotated
#           `Categoria (Military List)`, then `Tipologia`): stored on each row of the cell;
#           a total over blocks is checked against each block on its own (maintainer,
#           2026-10-24: two breakdowns of one total, one table). sum field
#           `<block>=<row>`: that block adds up to that row, not to the total (T23: the
#           imports' categories give MATERIALI, figure by figure; inferred from the
#           figures, the report does not say; maintainer, 2026-10-24)
#   companies  not printed: the ids of the companies a cell lists (sum field: that column),
#           a JSON list in printed order, null for a name with no id yet (an issue); the cell
#           is split by `lib/companies.split_list`. A name only a list prints never makes a
#           company by itself (maintainer, 2026-10-24: Difesa 4; any table that lists them)
#   rowsum  a row's own printed total of a year column (3B's `Nel quadriennio`), sum field
#           the column it adds: a printed figure, not a fact (`printed_figure` kind rowsum),
#   scale <col>  in the sum field of a year column: the unit printed after <col>'s value
#           (`2,591 Mrd`), stored as its multiplier (K 1.000, Mio 1.000.000, Mrd
#           1.000.000.000); <col> is stored scaled, its printed number in `<col>_raw`. The
#           year's cell prints value, unit and `rank` with no label each (MAE T6;
#   text    in the sum field of a year column: each year prints its own text there (MAE
#           T14.1's operator: each year its own top 15), stored as text
#   under <col>  in the sum field of a year column: printed on the line under <col>'s value,
#           in the same cell (MAE T1: each record's value over its count); a `Variaz. Y/Y-k`
#           column is stored on the row of year Y-k (maintainer, 2026-10-25)
#   colour <label>=<value>;...  in the sum field of a year column not printed: read from the
#           fill of the cell of the year's value, the colour the legend prints beside
#           <label>; <value> a column (all of that cell) or a number; no fill, 0. Flagged
#           `from the cell's colour` (MAE T15: orange `scadute`, yellow `di cui una
#   rank    in the sum field: a position printed in brackets, `(76)`, stored as 76
#   once    in the sum field: stored on the row of the edition's year only, NULL on the
#           others, so a sum is the printed one (3B's Importo, Residuo; maintainer, 2026-10-24)
#   bank    not printed: ArmTrace's id of the bank named in the column the sum field gives
#           (`lib/banks.py`: its name, the CAB left out; maintainer, 2026-10-25)
#   cab     not printed: the branch's CAB the bank's name prints, `(CAB 01600)` -> 01600
#   periods as `years`, each column a span of years (MAE T3 `2006-2010`): `anno_da`, `anno_a`
#   anno    a transposed table (MAE T9): each printed year column is one row, `anno` its
#           year; each printed row a measure column, known by the unit its cells print
#   none    the whole table is not imported (maintainer, 2026-10-25: charts): one line, no col
#   years   the printed year columns of a table that prints a year window (T2): one
#           row per printed row and year, `anno` + `valore` (amount). Several measures
#           per year (T10: `Anno 2022` over `N. | Valore in € | %`): one `years` line
#           per measure, labelled with the measure; the year is read from the label
#           over it (or under it: 3B's `INCASSO` over `2022`), `anno` is one column
#           (maintainer, 2026-10-24). `sum`: each year's cell is checked on its own
# event: a `date` column with sum field `event <WORD>` is filled on the rows of the list
#   headed `SOCIETA' <WORD> <year> (<n>)`: with the date the row prints, else the edition's
#   year (`2025`, nothing printed, flagged). A table with event columns is a register list
#   (`lib/extract.read_list`): numbered items, no grid (Difesa A5/2; maintainer, 2026-10-22:
#   no list column, no item number; the register across years is `registro_imprese`)
# labels: the printed header, `|` between the forms seen in different editions; a year is
#   written relative to the edition (`Y`, `Y-1`). Empty: the column prints no label.
# sum: `sum` when the column adds up to the table's printed totals and subtotals;
#   `sum else <col>@<col2>=<value>` when a blank cell counts as <col> on rows where
#   <col2> is <value> (MAE A1: an EUR authorisation leaves EURO blank, its value is
#   its Ammontare). `unless <col>`: a row where <col> is printed adds nothing (MAE A1:
#   a line with a customs value is not in the EURO subtotal; inferred from the subtotals,
#   and every one of the 159 matches it, to the cent or within conversion rounding).
